title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
description: Bone-in chicken brined overnight in salted buttermilk, then fried in a craggy, well-seasoned flour crust. Crisp outside, juicy to the bone.
notes: Thighs and drumsticks forgive more than breast. If you use breast, halve it so it cooks in the same time.

steps.text: Whisk the buttermilk with the salt, hot sauce, and garlic powder, submerge the chicken pieces, and refrigerate overnight.
steps.tip: The salt does the brining and the acid tenderises. Twelve hours is ideal; past a day the texture starts to turn soft.

steps.text: Mix the flour, cornstarch, paprika, cayenne, black pepper, salt, and baking powder. Rub in 3 tablespoons of the buttermilk brine with your fingers to make shaggy clumps.
steps.tip: Those clumps become the craggy crust. Without them the coating fries smooth and thin.

steps.text: Lift the chicken from the brine, let it drip, then press firmly into the coating on all sides. Rest on a rack while the oil heats.
steps.tip: Resting lets the coating hydrate and stick, so it does not fall off in the fryer.

steps.text: Fry in batches in a deep, heavy pot, turning occasionally, until the crust is deep brown and the thickest piece reads 74°C inside.
Drain on a rack and salt again while hot.
